intro: You are at Arsameia, an ancient city at Eski Kahta in Adıyaman province, whose story runs from the 3rd century BC to the 1st century AD. This was the royal cult centre of the Kingdom of Commagene, and it is famous for one image above all: the colossal Mithridates relief.
history: Arsameia was the sacred seat of King Mithridates I Kallinikos, and his son Antiochus I expanded it. With its tunnel, its palace ruins and its six-metre relief, it is the second most important site of Commagene.
structure-1: You are now in front of the Mithridates Relief. This six-metre relief depicts King Mithridates I standing with Herakles. Look closely at the two figures, a king and a god face to face.
structure-2: Here is the Sacred Tunnel: 158 metres of steps cut into the rock, leading down from the sacred precinct. Imagine descending into the darkness of the mountain, step after step.
structure-4: Now look at the Rock Inscriptions. Royal and sacred texts were carved straight into the rock here, so that the words would last as long as the mountain.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Palace Ruins and the Agora.
facts: Did you know? The relief of Mithridates here is one of the largest relief carvings in Anatolia. Arsameia was the summer capital of Commagene: Antiochus, whose tomb crowns Nemrut, made it a sanctuary for his father Mithridates. The relief of Heracles shaking hands with King Mithridates is the best-preserved Commagene work, and god and king are shown the same height. And the 158-metre shaft cut straight into the rock remains a structure whose purpose is still not fully understood.
outro: This brings our tour of Arsameia to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. A king and a god have shaken hands here for centuries; let them keep greeting those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
